record.paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
record.original_question: What general mathematical connection links controllability theory and optimal control theory for stochastic distributed parameter systems, especially for problems with endpoint state constraints, and how can the initial finite-codimensional exact controllability results be extended into a broader theory?

evidence.quote: (12) The connection between controllability and optimal control. The survey divides itself naturally into two parts—controllability and optimal control. There should be a close ...

relationship between these two topics. Some initial findings are given in [24], in which a new link between (finite-codimensional exact) controllability and optimal control problems for SDPSs with endpoint state constraints is presented. However, lots of things are to be done, which are by no means easy tasks.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a stochastic distributed parameter system (SDPS) of the form
   dy(t) = (A y(t) + B u(t)) dt + (C y(t) + D u(t)) dW(t),  t ∈ (0, T],   y(0) = y₀,
on a separable Hilbert space H, where A generates a C₀-semigroup, B, C, D are suitable (possibly unbounded) linear operators, W is a one-dimensional standard Brownian motion on a filtered probability space, the control u belongs to an admissible set U_ad ⊂ L²_F(0,T; U) (U a Hilbert space), and the state y is an H-valued adapted process. Given a closed subspace (or convex set) Q ⊂ L²_{F_T}(Ω; H) representing endpoint state constraints y(T) ∈ Q, and a cost functional
   J(u) = E[ ∫₀ᵀ ℓ(t, y(t), u(t)) dt + h(y(T)) ],
the system is said to be finite-codimensional exactly controllable (with respect to a finite-codimensional subspace of H) at time T if the reachable set {y(T; u) : u ∈ U_ad} contains an affine subspace of finite codimension in L²_{F_T}(Ω; H).

Develop a general theory linking controllability and optimal control for such SDPS with endpoint state constraints by accomplishing the following:

(a) Formulate and prove a Pontryagin-type maximum principle for optimal controls of the constrained problem (minimize J over u ∈ U_ad subject to y(T) ∈ Q) in which the nontriviality of the adjoint variables is guaranteed precisely by a finite-codimensional exact controllability property of the linearized SDPS along the optimal trajectory.

(b) Identify sharp sufficient conditions (in terms of observability/Gårding-type inequalities for the associated backward stochastic adjoint equation) under which finite-codimensional exact controllability of the linearized SDPS holds, and show how these conditions yield the nontriviality of the Lagrange multipliers in (a).

(c) Extend the theory beyond the linear setting (semilinear/quasilinear SDPS, degenerate noise, unbounded control operators) and derive analogous equivalences between qualitative controllability properties and the well-posedness/nontriviality of first- and second-order necessary optimality conditions for endpoint-constrained stochastic optimal control problems.
artifact.status_search_result: Initial findings linking finite-codimensional exact controllability with optimal control problems with endpoint state constraints (in the deterministic setting) appear in Wang–Yong–Zhang (J. Math. Pures Appl., 2020; arXiv:1810.01334), where the connection is reduced to a Gårding-type inequality for the adjoint system. A general theory for stochastic distributed parameter systems is acknowledged as an open program; the recent monograph "Mathematical Control Theory for Stochastic Partial Differential Equations" (Springer, 2021) and surveys describe many directions still to be developed. No comprehensive resolution has been published.

status_evidence.title: Finite Codimensional Controllability, and Optimal Control Problems with Endpoint State Constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Finite codimensional (exact/approximate) controllability is introduced, motivated by the study of optimal control problems for infinite dimensional systems with endpoint state constraints; reduced to a Gårding-type inequality for the adjoint system.
status_evidence.claim: Initial deterministic results establishing the link, leaving the stochastic and general theory open.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical Control Theory for Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
status_evidence.snippet: First book to systematically present control theory for stochastic distributed parameter systems; explains new phenomena and difficulties in controllability and optimal control problems.
status_evidence.claim: Comprehensive theory bridging controllability and optimal control for SDPS with endpoint constraints is identified as an ongoing research program.
